model_annotation: The bar chart on the left illustrates the percentage of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) attributed to the federal government (Bund), the states (Länder), and municipalities (Gemeinden) in Germany from 1991 to 2023. The vertical axis represents the percentage of GDP, ranging from -0.5% to 3.5%, with a linear scale. The horizontal axis shows the years in intervals of five, from 1991 to 2023. The bars are color-coded: blue for the federal government, purple for the states, and green for the municipalities. The bars are grouped by year, with each bar representing the combined contribution of the three levels of government to the GDP for that year. The chart also includes a black line that represents the total contribution of all levels of government to the GDP, which is labeled as "Bundreform2." The bars are not sorted in any specific order, and there are no bars that are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining. The chart on the right is a line chart that shows the same data as the bar chart on the left, with the same axes and labels. The line chart includes a black line representing the total contribution of all levels of government to the GDP, labeled as "Bundreform2." The line chart also includes bars for each level of government, color-coded similarly to the bar chart on the left. The bars in the line chart are not sorted, and there are no bars that are visually emphasized.
